Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 7 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR (per source-fidelity note). Ch 7 likely develops VIRTUE AND SPIRITUAL FORMATION as the soul-preparation catalog. The virtue-and-spiritual-formation pedagogy parallels the standard patristic-monastic catechetical structure: EVAGRIUS PONTICUS Praktikos §§6-89 (the eight evil thoughts + the virtue-catalog); JOHN CASSIAN Conferences (the foundational Latin monastic catechesis); JOHN CLIMACUS The Ladder of Divine Ascent (the thirty-step monastic-spiritual-progression — translated into Geʽez as Mäṣḥafä Märet Awalda); BASIL Asketikon (the foundational Greek monastic rule); APOPHTHEGMATA PATRUM (the Desert Fathers' sayings preserved in Tewahedo Mäṣḥafä Anṣaraye). The Tewahedo monastic tradition (Däbrä Damo + Däbrä Libanos + Däbrä Hayq Istifanos monasteries' catechetical pedagogy) preserves the virtue-and-spiritual-formation catalog as the integral-soul-preparation rubric.

HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of HUMILITY as FOUNDATIONAL VIRTUE inverting the Devil's-pride (seed 4:5 'You became proud; you were CALLED the Devil'). The humility theme parallels: MATTHEW 5:3 ('blessed are the poor in spirit'); MATTHEW 23:12 ('whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted'); LUKE 14:11 + 18:14 (the same humility-exaltation reversal); PHILIPPIANS 2:5-11 (the Christ-emptying-himself kenosis-hymn — the foundational humility Christology); JAMES 4:6 + 1 PETER 5:5 ('God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble'); PSALM 51:17 ('a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise'); JOHN CLIMACUS Ladder Step 25 (humility as the most-extensive treatment in the Ladder). Tewahedo monastic-tradition preserves humility as the PREREQUISITE-CONDITION for receiving the complete-repentance four-step rubric (seed 4:34).
